newsitem.title: GERMANY: German government spokesman statement on forex.
newsitem.headline: German government spokesman statement on forex.

text.p: Here is the full statement by German government spokesman Peter Hausmann on the cabinet discussion on Wednesday about foreign exchange developments.
Hausmann was reading from a prepared text after being asked to comment on the issue by journalists attending the government's regular news conference.
"It is correct that the cabinet today briefly discussed the foreign exchange markets and the situation on the foreign exchange markets.

"There was a report by the federal finance minister and the discussion came to the conclusion that from a German perspective there is no reason to dramatise recent developments on foreign exchange markets.

"The rise of the dollar and the pound should be seen against the backdrop of economic developments in the United States and Britain. Speculative effects ahead of economic and monetary union could also have led to an overreaction on markets. Chancellor (Helmut) Kohl again made clear that the euro will come on time and that it will be a strong currency.

"The G7 finance ministers and central bank governors had already stated at their meeting in Berlin on February 8 of this year that the, and I quote, 'considerable mistaken developments on foreign exchange markets' had been corrected. The German government is in close contact with its G7 partners and will continue to closely oberserve developments on foreign exchange markets. All of the G7 countries stand behind the position that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and significant deviation from these fundamentals are not desirable."
